purpose: Evidence-controlled reconstruction of the changing physical footprint of 600 Stockton Street.

evidence_rules.documented: Directly visible or measurable in a primary source.
evidence_rules.supported: Supported by multiple reliable sources but not directly measured from an original plan.
evidence_rules.approximate: A published or inferred measurement that requires verification.
evidence_rules.reconstructed: Historically informed interpretation rather than surviving original documentation.

periods.research_note: The pre-1909 site condition should be digitized directly from the historic Sanborn map. No geometry is entered until it is measured.

periods.building_name: Metropolitan Life Insurance Company Pacific Coast Head Office
periods.research_note: The original 1909 footprint is documented as a smaller rectangular Stockton-facing structure. Exact geometry must be established from primary cartographic or architectural evidence before coordinates are assigned.
This period should be used to compare the Sanborn footprint with contemporary photographs and identify the relationship between the original core and early additions.
The 1919 map documents a substantially expanded complex. Exact geometry and dimensions will be extracted from the original map.
The research identifies major expansion activity during this period, but individual footprint changes require primary-source verification.
Later additions completed the mature multi-wing complex. Individual construction campaigns require separate documentation.
